harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Established a persistent SHA-256 integrity baseline for `/etc` on node1. The checker reports added, removed, content-changed, and metadata-changed paths, runs daily through cron, and survived a verified node restart. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created a protected root-owned baseline containing 1,318 entries.
Excluded four boot/runtime-derived files (`adjtime`, `aliases.db`, and two blkid cache files) to avoid routine false positives; their authoritative configuration sources remain monitored.
Verified detection using controlled temporary files and retained timestamped reports under `/var/log/etc-integrity`.
Restarted node1 once and verified its changed boot identity, recovered cron service, persisted data, and clean final integrity state.

evidence.requirement: Establish an `/etc` integrity baseline compatible with the installed legacy OS
evidence.summary: Confirmed CentOS 5.11/kernel 2.6.18, installed a coreutils-based checker, and initialized a clean 1,318-entry baseline.
Controlled additions were reported with path, metadata, and SHA-256 fingerprint and returned alert status 1. Test files were removed, three reports persisted, and the final check was clean.

evidence.requirement: Run checks regularly and protect integrity data
evidence.summary: The daily cron hook and checker are root-owned mode 700; the baseline is root-owned mode 600; crond is running and enabled in normal runlevels.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart persistence and recovery
evidence.summary: Captured healthy pre-restart state, received reboot acknowledgement, proved boot ID changed from fcfb529e-f300-44b0-8000-000000000000 to 0ef097c3-f9ae-4ac1-8000-000000000000, and verified recovered crond, unchanged OS/kernel, persisted baseline and reports, and a clean post-restart check.
